top_signal.title: How would you build a sales pipeline for a ~$180K IT services company with no established sales network?
top_signal.summary: I'm a co-founder of a small tech services company in India, currently doing around ₹1.5 crore (~$180K) in business. We work across data engineering, analytics, and AI.   We've managed to get here without a formal sales function. Most of our existing clients came from relationships and people we'd worked with previously. We've built a solid delivery team and have proven that we can deliver, but now we're struggling with the next challenge: building a predictable sales pipeline beyond our existing network.   The problem is that none of our founding team has a strong industry network or a background in enterprise sales. We're technical founders who figured out how to build the business, but selling consistently to new enterprise clients is a different game.   Here's what I've been considering:      Outbound prospecting:  Cold email and LinkedIn outreach, although I'm skeptical about how effective these are for landing enterprise IT services contracts without referrals or credibility.    Outsourced sales agencies:  Not sure whether they can actually sell complex technical services or will just generate low-quality meetings.    Hiring a senior sales leader:  The compensation expectations of someone experienced enough to bring enterprise deals could eat up a significant portion of our revenue.
